tools.name: keys.create
tools.description: Mint a pf_ caller key bound to one HoldKit namespace.

tools.name: inbox.create
tools.description: Create an inbox. Returns webhook and A2A URLs.

tools.name: inbox.poll
tools.description: Read inbox events after a cursor.

tools.name: inbox.wait
tools.description: Poll an inbox. block_ms is accepted and capped at 0 in this MVP, so the call returns current events.

tools.name: timer.set
tools.description: Schedule a durable timer. Delivery URLs must be public https.

tools.name: lock.acquire
tools.description: Take a lease lock. Returns a fencing token.

tools.name: lock.release
tools.description: Release a lock with its fencing token.

tools.name: idem.begin
tools.description: Start an idempotency key or return the prior outcome. fingerprint is a hex hash.

tools.name: idem.commit
tools.description: Store the outcome reference for an idempotency key. scope (max 64) and owner are optional. When owner is omitted, the caller key hash is sent.

tools.name: kv.set
tools.description: Write a small value with a TTL. Emails and card numbers are rejected.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: inbox.poll · Private data: lock.acquire, lock.release · Public sink: inbox.create · Destructive: kv.delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: inbox.poll · Private data: lock.acquire, lock.release · Public sink: inbox.create · Destructive: kv.delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
